claims.evidence: Northwind Robotics reported third-quarter revenue of $412 million for the quarter ended September 30; it does not say the results were announced on Thursday.
revenue of $412 million for the quarter ended September 30, up 23% year-over-year
above analyst expectations of $389 million
Net income rose to $47.2 million, or $0.94 per diluted share, from $31.5 million, or $0.63 per share, a year earlier.

"We are seeing unprecedented demand for our autonomous fulfillment systems," said CEO Marta Lindqvist during the earnings call. "Our order backlog now stands at $1.8 billion, which gives us exceptional visibility into 2027."
Revenue from the company's flagship PickStream platform grew 61%
the services segment expanded 18%
International sales accounted for 34% of total revenue, up from 28% a year ago
Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 43.1%.
CFO David Chen attributed the decline to elevated component costs and tariff-related pressures.
The company also announced a 3% workforce reduction, affecting approximately 210 positions, as part of a broader restructuring initiative expected to save $25 million annually.
Northwind raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.58 billion to $1.62 billion, from $1.52 billion to $1.57 billion previously.
Shares rose 6.8% in after-hours trading following the announcement.
